args.prompt:
Use the attached clay render as the exact blueprint. Keep every wall, opening, window, cornice, skirting, floor and ceiling line, the camera height, lens and angle, and the position, size and angle of every furniture piece and built-in exactly as in the clay. Move, resize, add or remove nothing. Each placeholder shape in the clay marks one product listed below; render it there at the stated size. Only turn the clay into real materials and light. The other attached images are close-ups of the exact products: match their form, colour and texture. Positions are fractions of frame width (x) and height (y) from the top-left.

1. PHOTO. Top Scandinavian interiors magazine: a small Nordic study, 3 pm mid-winter, 24 mm shift lens at 1.1 m, level, one-point symmetric, all sharp. Hero at first glance, dead centre: the built-in oak desk and shelf on a calm white wall, generous bare wall between them, the light drawing the composition.

2. LIGHT. One key: soft north daylight from the window on the left wall, no sun; outside, bare birches, no snow, no buildings. No lamp is lit. Exposed for white: the desk wall by the left corner clean white, a step under the glowing reveal; the glass brightest, detailed. Light rakes across the desk wall from the left and falls off smoothly half a stop to the right corner; the right wall in soft shade. The shelf draws a soft shadow line on the wall below it; chair and desk cast long soft shadows right and toward the camera; the plant's leaves glow against the window; dense contact shadows under the baskets. Ceiling a touch darker, darkest top right. Real contrast, never milky. 4600 K: whites white, never cream, pink or grey.

3. MATERIALS. Matte mineral paint #F4F1EC, faint chalky movement in the raking light. Wide oiled white-oak planks, pale honey #D6BF9E. Built-in desk with a drawer, floating shelf and chair: oiled light oak #C8A27A, satin sheen, a long soft window highlight along the desk top.

4. PRODUCTS, one per line, each on its clay placeholder:
a. CURTAIN, cut by the left edge: near stack of a sheer oat linen-look panel, visible slub, soft deep waves from rings on a slim black rod under the cornice, hem on the floor, backlit.
b. RUG under the chair, cut by the bottom edge: white hand-woven flat wool rug, tone-on-tone diamond weave, fine grey flecks.
c. BASKET under the desk, left: empty cream cotton rope basket, about the chair seat's height.
d. BIN under the desk, right: mist-grey washable kraft-paper bin, rolled cuff, a little lower than the chair seat.
e. PLANTER in the corner by the window: a 38 cm natural seagrass belly basket as a pot cover, an upright soft-leaved plant in it, crown below the shelf.
f. FELT BINS at both shelf ends: two light-grey felt open bins, palm-height; the shelf centre bare.
g. PEN CUP on the desk, left: hand-sized white speckled stone cup, 4-6 natural wood pencils; the rest of the desk bare.

5. NOT IN FRAME: artwork, bookends, books, ceiling lamp, wall lamp, desk lamp, tray, magazines, laptop, papers, mirror, glass, socket, cable, text, people. No sun patches, beams, bloom, haze, halos, HDR, grain or vignette.
